topics.title: AT&T Troubles and a Disappearing Date
topics.summary: Howard struggles with static on his phone line while interviewing Elephant Boy about a disastrous date where the girl vanished after one encounter. The conversation devolves into frustration over AT&T service, misinterpretations of the caller’s voice, and general communication difficulties.

topics.title: Radio Callers Discuss a Controlling Wife
topics.summary: A radio program features callers discussing an unnamed woman’s excessive control and critical behavior towards her husband, focusing on her meticulous meal preparation habits contrasted with her inability to perform simple tasks like making coffee. The conversation explores the unusual dynamic of their relationship.

topics.title: Family Conflict & Garage Living
topics.summary: A tense phone call reveals a dysfunctional family dynamic, with accusations of infidelity and neglect leveled against one member who lives in the garage while his partner doesn’t reciprocate affection. The conversation includes uncomfortable details about the individual's upbringing and attempts to secure concert tickets amidst heated arguments.

topics.title: Howard Stern’s Unfiltered Callers
topics.summary: During an on-air segment, Howard Stern engages in a highly confrontational and often bizarre conversation with numerous callers. He repeatedly insults individuals based on their appearance or personal situations using crude language and outlandish accusations, leading to shouting matches and absurd pronouncements as he aggressively questions the callers.

topics.title: Stern’s Callers and Rosewood Bitterness
topics.summary: During a radio broadcast, Howard Stern expresses frustration with callers who fail to understand his jokes or offer helpful input. The show concludes with an extended musical performance featuring multiple songs centered around the theme of rosewood bitterness.

topics.title: Repetitive Phrase Broadcast
topics.summary: The broadcast consists primarily of repeated phrases – "Helped me through the times when I feel blue" – interspersed with unrelated comments about a roadie, personal relationships, family members, and a lengthy recitation of a children’s poem about a miniature rodeo parakeet. The speaker also discusses their grandmother's support for their lesbian identity and shares anecdotes regarding their relatives.
